summary: Simultaneous operations span multiple Middle East fronts: IDF strikes killed Hamas and PIJ operatives in Gaza, forces conducted raids in the West Bank, and strikes were reported in southern Lebanon. Houthi-US talks occurred in Muscat with Houthis pledging no attacks on US ships. Strikes were reported in Iranian Kurdistan amid the anniversary of Jina Mahsa Amini's killing.

Saudi Arabia preparing to restore half of attacked east-west oil pipeline capacity within days, full recovery expected in approximately six weeks. (Source: @asafroz/53497)
IDF strikes reported in southern Lebanon; artillery shelling and drone activity concentrated in Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil, and Marjayoun areas with 126 total alerts recorded. (Source: @redlinkleb/43396)
Strikes reported in Iranian Kurdistan on anniversary of Jina Mahsa Amini killing; Iranian forces closed road to Aichi Cemetery in Saqqez. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/7174)

sections.threat_assessment: The Houthi threat to Saudi and US interests remains active with a ballistic missile intercepted over Mecca and continued FPV drone use along the Marib front. The US-Houthi contact in Muscat suggests a potential de-escalation channel, though Houthi commitments to avoid US ships and commercial vessels remain unverified. Iranian Kurdish strikes and UAV activity near the Iraqi border indicate Tehran-linked operations expanding beyond Syria. The IDF's simultaneous operations in Gaza, West Bank, and reported strikes in Lebanon suggest a multi-front security posture that could escalate further.
sections.regional_response: Turkey condemned the Houthi missile attack on Mecca within the framework of the Saudi-Turkey security cooperation agreement. Algeria closed its airspace to all UAE flights effective September 11, signaling a diplomatic or security rift. Jordan saw renewed unrest over Gaza and Amman's policy toward Israel. The US offered intelligence but not military support to Saudi Arabia against Houthis, while Oman served as intermediary in US-Houthi talks.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Houthi pledge to avoid attacking US ships and commercial vessels (except Saudi-linked) during the Muscat talks requires verification through subsequent behavior monitoring. The Duvdevan Unit's capture of a senior PIJ figure in Burqin indicates continued Shin Bet intelligence sharing and Israeli operational depth in the West Bank. The Kirkuk oil fire and Algeria-UAE airspace closure suggest expanding regional instability beyond the primary conflict zones. Low Hormuz traffic (4 ships vs 18 average) may indicate maritime security concerns or rerouting.
